title: Luca e Chiara
coverAlt: A watercolour of the two of us kissing on a stone stair, lemons overhead and a Vespa at the foot
lede: Embark on an unforgettable journey through the enchanting streets of Rome and the artistic wonders of Florence! Immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of history that these cities offer, as you stroll past ancient ruins and magnificent architecture. Indulge in mouthwatering Italian cuisine, from authentic pasta dishes to delectable gelato, and savor every bite. Marvel at iconic landmarks such as the majestic Colosseum and the renowned Uffizi Gallery, where masterpieces await your admiration. Experience the vibrant atmosphere of local markets, bustling with life and color, and take in the serene beauty of the picturesque Tuscan countryside, dotted with charming villages and rolling hills. This trip promises to be a true feast for the senses, filled with culture, art, and unforgettable memories that will last a lifetime. Don’t let this incredible adventure pass you by!

days.title: The Atlantic
blurb: Left Atlanta on the evening flight with two cameras and no plan past the first morning.
Eight hours over the Atlantic, most of them awake.

days.title: St. Peter’s Basilica
blurb: Into the Vatican before the queue had properly formed.
Spent longer on the colonnade than inside it, which felt like the right mistake to make.

days.title: The Forum & Colloseum
blurb: The Forum in the afternoon heat, then the Colosseum as the light went.
Rented e-bikes after dark and rode the whole thing again with nobody in it.

exif.lens: iPhone 17 Pro back triple camera 6.765mm f/1.78

days.title: Pompeii & Mt. Vesuvius
blurb: Train south, then Pompeii from the Porta Marina gate.
Vesuvius sat there the whole time doing nothing in particular.

days.title: The Apian Way
blurb: Out along the Appia Antica on bikes, aqueduct on the left the entire way.
Umbrella pines, cobbles older than most countries.

days.title: Piazza Vechio
blurb: Florence by mid-morning. Straight to the Piazza della Signoria.
Stood under the Neptune fountain until it made sense.

days.title: Galileo, Da Vinci, & Baboli
blurb: Science museum first, then the Boboli gardens with the sun coming straight down the cypress avenue.
Best light of the trip and I nearly missed it.

days.title: Duomo di Santa Maria del Fiore
blurb: Climbed the Duomo. Regretted it on the stairs, forgot about it at the top.
Marble in three colours and none of them quite what the photos promise.

frames.alt: Duomo di Santa Maria del Fiore

days.title: Castel Sant’Angelo
blurb: Back in Rome. Crossed the Ponte Sant’Angelo with the Bernini angels doing their thing.
Castle first, terrace after.

days.title: Pantheon, Vicus Caprarius
blurb: Pantheon at opening, before the floor filled.
Then down into the Vicus Caprarius, an entire Roman street sitting under a cinema.

days.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
blurb: Last full day. Doria Pamphilj, which almost nobody goes to.
A hall of mirrors and about four hundred paintings hung four deep.

days.title: Bonus
blurb: Everything that did not belong to a single day.
Mostly granita, mostly at the wrong time of the afternoon.
